source.author: verg
source.text: Tum canit, errantem Permessi ad flumina Gallum Aonas in montis ut duxerit una sororum, utque viro Phoebi chorus assurrexerit omnis; ut Linus haec illi, divino carmine pastor, floribus atque apio crinis ornatus amaro, dixerit:
source.text_original: Tum canit, errantem Permessi ad flumina Gallum / Aonas in montis ut duxerit una sororum, / utque viro Phoebi chorus assurrexerit omnis; / ut Linus haec illi, divino carmine pastor, / floribus atque apio crinis ornatus amaro, / dixerit:
source.text_english: Then he sings how one of the sisters led Gallus, wandering to the streams of Permessus, to the Aonian mountains, and how the whole choir of Phoebus rose up to the man; and how Linus, the shepherd, with divine song, his hair adorned with flowers and bitter celery, said these things to him:

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: o si mihi liceret istius modi ingenium non per Aonios montes et Heliconis uertices, ut poetae canunt, sed per Sion et Itabyrium et Sina et excelsa ducere scripturarum, si contingeret docere, quae didici, et quasi per manus mysteria tradere prophetarum, nasceretur nobis aliquid, quod docta Graecia non haberet.
reuse.text_original: o si mihi liceret istius modi ingenium non per Aonios montes et Heliconis uertices, ut poetae canunt, sed per Sion et Itabyrium et Sina et excelsa ducere scripturarum, si contingeret docere, quae didici, et quasi per manus mysteria tradere prophetarum, nasceretur nobis aliquid, quod docta Graecia non haberet.
reuse.text_english: O if it were permitted me to lead a mind of this sort, not through the Aonian mountains and the peaks of Helicon, as the poets sing, but through Sion and Itabyrium and Sina and the heights of the Scriptures; if it were possible to teach what I have learned and, as it were, hand on the mysteries of the prophets from hand to hand, something would arise among us that learned Greece would not possess.
